sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 are sitting at the top of their one-month range, both closing 2026-09-22 at their highest marks of the past month (S&P 7,764.64; Nasdaq 100 30,732.40). The VIX sits at the low end of its one-month band (14.21, versus a high of 17.84), consistent with a market not pricing near-term stress. The Euro Stoxx 50 is the outlier, sitting in the lower third of its one-month range at 6,324.72 versus a high of 6,485.67. Into that backdrop, 22 earnings events land this week, concentrated across industrials, technology, financial-services, healthcare and consumer names.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Tuesday is the week's heaviest earnings day: Hexcel (HXL US) reports into industrials, the softest-reacting sector with earnings this week at a -1.43% median off recent prints, while Elevance Health (ELV US) reports the same day into healthcare, a roughly flat group at +0.11% median. Monday opens with Jefferies (JEF US) into financial-services (+0.195% median). Wednesday brings Micron (MU US) into technology, the strongest positive-reacting group in this pool at +0.87% median. Thursday closes the week with McCormick (MKC US) into consumer-defensive, sitting at -0.54% median.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining leads the sector reaction table this week at +6.62% median across 176 tickers, backed by a thick news window (2,630 items). Alternative-asset-management follows at +2.925% median (6 tickers, 238 news items) and copper at +2.63% median (6 tickers, 248 news items), both far thinner-covered than mining. None of this week's scheduled reporters sit directly in these three sectors, so treat them as backdrop context, not a preview of this week's prints.
